feedback_interpretation: H24 is strengthened as limited structural transfer: at 100 ul, m89 grows from 8.81/14.05 at 5/1 to 13.49/26.04 ml at 10/1, whereas m104 changes from 5.20/13.90 to 7.91/11.00. m86 retains steep 5/1 response across loading, but full invariance is rejected by a 50-to-150 ul change of -5.25/-1.31 ml; completion is comparatively stable while onset advances. These questions now have lower marginal priority. H18 requires revision: transfer of m194's completion decline to 50 ul is rejected by its rising 10.34/14.73/21.52 ml sequence across 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1, unlike the 100 ul 36.18-to-28.27 decline. The actual m20 baseline is now measured and connects an increasing fixed-50 ul curve; the older m148 attribution remains discarded. m106 supports stronger later growth rather than the historically forecast early rise. H13 gains qualified support: m61's 2/1-to-10/1 onset change is -2.32 ml at 50 ul and -9.30 at 100 ul, while completion changes are similar at -4.63 and -4.75 ml. This rejects a large loading-invariant inverse onset response and supports separate endpoint interactions. H15 is refined by modest m25 growth through 10/1 before its large 50/1 anchor and opposite historical completion-error signs across m25, m82 and m95, rejecting a shared beta-ketoester correction. H25's initial m45 and m96 curve questions are substantially answered. H17's proposed large early lactone completion tail is unsupported: m181 at 50 ul measures 6.18/10.19, 7.38/13.29 and 21.45/31.79 ml at 1/1, 2/1 and 10/1, leaving a specific intermediate-ratio question. m177 still rejects smooth loading interpolation, but available lower-ratio inputs cannot replicate its exceptional high-ratio minima. Repeated short m92 EA completion supports a local association while PE-side repeatability remains unresolved. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over their measured ranges. All measured findings come from observed-table records; historical residuals describe past failures and candidate matches remain predictions only. No new labels, validation/test truth or external trajectory information were used.
batch_rationale: The latest feedback favors a few remaining conditional anchors followed by broader response learning. m194 receives a controlled 150 ul sequence, m61 a targeted third-loading anchor, m25 a later-ratio pair with a loading bridge, and m181 an intermediate transition measurement. The remaining choices build connected curves across aminoester conjugation, alcohol topology, hydroxyaldehydes, ether acrylates, hydrophobic esters, phenylmalonate, boronate and basic nitrogen. The m75 group forms a two-ratio, two-loading comparison with an observed anchor. These experiments expand condition coverage within observed identities while avoiding routine completion of already mapped surfaces.

important_observations.statement: m177 is an exceptional, strongly non-smooth surface. At 50/1, V2 is 59.88, 7.31 and 81.30 ml at 50, 100 and 150 ul. At 100 ul, V2 is 19.18, 20.70 and 7.31 ml at 5/1, 10/1 and 50/1; V1 remains near 5 ml. The measured 5/1, 50 ul and 20/1, 50 ul points are 14.51 and 8.50 ml in V2. These observations reject simple loading interpolation. A reproducible conditional minimum and omitted experimental variation remain competing hypotheses.

m194 changes response shape with loading. At 100 ul, completion decreases from 36.18 to 28.27 ml between 1/1 and 2/1 with nearly fixed onset. At 50 ul, the corresponding measured sequence is 10.34, 14.73 and 21.52 ml at 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1. A common ratio correction or monotone loading term is inadequate.

The corrected fixed-50 ul m20 curve rises from 7.70/10.73 at 1/1 to 10.80/15.09 at 2/1, 15.84/22.69 at 5/1 and 23.78/34.90 at 10/1. The previously attributed low-ratio observation was m148, so the actual m20 baseline is now measured and the earlier shoulder interpretation is rejected.

m106 now has a connected fixed-100 ul sequence: 6.23/10.54, 7.16/13.39, 20.86/42.52 and 41.72/79.81 ml at 1/1, 2/1, 10/1 and 20/1. This supports a delayed joint transition in an ether-containing ketone, while the historical 10/1 prediction substantially overstated both endpoints.

Aminoester transfer is local. m86 and m88 show substantial joint endpoint growth by 5/1 under their fixed 100 ul DCM conditions, whereas m89 remains moderate through 10/1 under PE loading and m104 has a moderate 5/1-to-10/1 response. Different loading solvent, plug volume, density and substitution environment prevent attributing the contrast to amino position alone.

Alcohol response is heterogeneous: fixed-50 ul m60 grows strongly with ratio, while fixed-100 ul m61 onset decreases from 12.34 to 3.04 ml across 2/1 to 10/1. The m61 50 ul pair shows a much smaller change. A shared alcohol correction is unsupported.

Identical m92 1/1, 50 ul, EA-loaded inputs give 5.18/12.01 and 5.72/11.70 ml, while the single PE-loaded counterpart gives 8.02/20.57 ml. This supports local persistence of the short EA completion, but PE-side repeatability and a general solvent-identity effect remain untested.

Increasing EA fraction generally strengthens normal-phase silica elution. Donor accessibility, basic nitrogen, hydrogen bonding, injection-solvent focusing and adsorption can modify this locally. These are chemical priors and are not established causes of any measured anomaly.

possible_model_blind_spots.statement: A single molecular offset, global loading term or smooth monotone ratio interpolation cannot represent the m177, m194 and m61 surfaces. V1 and V2 need separate molecule-by-condition interactions.

Functional-group counts and broad polarity descriptors do not reliably transfer response shapes: aminoesters, alcohols, ether carbonyls and beta-ketoesters with similar HBD/HBA patterns occupy different regimes.

Some current candidate outputs have non-monotone or incoherent predicted quantiles, including q50 values outside the q10-to-q90 ordering. This indicates output-calibration or representation issues, but quantile width is not measured uncertainty and does not establish expected learning value.

Loading amount, sample volume, loading-solvent identity, plug volume and density are strongly entangled in the pool. A model may learn spurious global effects unless these are represented as conditional features and evaluated with matched complete tuples.

The adaptively sampled pool is rich in exceptional high-tail surfaces. Overall Row accuracy may still be limited by ordinary moderate-response chemistry and lower-ratio condition coverage; historical residual magnitude alone cannot establish Row prevalence.

Audit training-only fit by molecule, ratio, loading and endpoint before assuming more nearby labels will solve every error. Audit raw outputs, transformations and serialization for endpoint and quantile inconsistencies without spending labels. Global monotonicity in ratio or loading is unsupported by these measured surfaces. Replicate-aware analysis should separate repeated-input variation from new-condition residuals; unusual singleton labels should neither be automatically discarded nor treated as deterministic.

hypotheses.content: Ether/carbonyl response depends on molecular environment and loading. m194 completion rises across 1/1-to-5/1 at 50 ul but falls from 1/1 to 2/1 at 100 ul. The corrected m20 curve grows jointly, while m106 develops stronger growth later.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched m194 anchors constrain completion-specific interactions; m21 and m114 test transfer to less sampled ether/carbonyl surfaces.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m194 retain its completion decline at 150 ul, and do phenoxyacrylate and diaryl-ketone lower-ratio labels follow nearby measured response shapes?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol ratio response depends on loading and endpoint. m61 onset decreases only 2.32 ml from 2/1 to 10/1 at 50 ul versus 9.30 ml at 100 ul, while completion decreases similarly. Other alcohols show strong growth; exceptional m120 and m207 inputs remain unreplicated.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The remaining m61 anchor and connected primary- and nitro-alcohol curves distinguish onset interactions from completion slopes and limit inappropriate alcohol-wide transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 ul, does m61 onset already decrease by 5/1, and do m204 and m200 exhibit joint growth or endpoint decoupling?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl arrangement limits transfer across beta-ketoesters and diesters. m25 grows modestly through 10/1 before its large measured 50/1 response; m82 and m95 have different 10/1 regimes. Phenylmalonate ratio and loading responses cannot be inferred from shallow m80 behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A later m25 increment and a controlled m75 loading comparison teach transition location and structural limits without propagating a shared polycarbonyl correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How much does m25 grow from 10/1 to 20/1 at 150 ul, and does the m75 loading effect change between 2/1 and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Lactone and ketone arrangements have different endpoint slopes. m181 has modest low-ratio endpoints followed by joint growth at 10/1, whereas m179 retains shallow onset. m40 grows jointly between its measured 2/1 and 10/1 anchors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m181 intermediate point and matched m40 baseline distinguish transition shape from molecular offset across ordinary cyclic and fused carbonyl environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m181 begin joint growth by 5/1, and is m40's lower-ratio progression shallow before its measured higher-ratio rise?

hypotheses.content: Ortho-hydroxyaryl aldehydes may occupy different ratio-response regimes despite shared donor and carbonyl groups. m190 retains onset near 6 ml through 10/1 while completion grows; sparse m117 and m186 anchors do not establish the same slope. Substitution and injection context remain entangled.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled hydroxyaldehyde curves test whether completion-dominated or joint growth transfers appropriately across related donor/carbonyl environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m117 and m186 develop substantial onset growth, or preserve early onset while completion increases, under their own fixed injection conditions?

hypotheses.content: Hydrophobic acrylate ester environments may have different ratio sensitivity from the larger measured ether-acrylate response. Pure-EA m15 and m16 anchors establish low-ratio endpoints but do not determine their PE-enrichment slopes. Cross-molecule comparisons retain the selected loading differences.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Parallel fixed-loading curves broaden ordinary ester coverage and test whether recently acquired polar acrylate responses transfer excessively.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Across 1/1 to 10/1, do cyclohexyl acrylate at 100 ul and branched alkyl acrylate at 150 ul remain modest, grow jointly, or differ primarily in completion?

The m75 group forms a two-ratio, two-loading comparison with an observed anchor. These experiments expand condition coverage within observed identities while avoiding routine completion of already mapped surfaces.

The conditional anchors address consequential interpolation questions; less sampled curves test transfer across chemically distinct Row environments at modest and larger endpoint scales. Small measured changes would also teach useful local invariance. The supplied trajectory does not support a numerical estimate of retrained overall Row accuracy gain, and these new conditions cannot resolve repeatability of existing exceptional inputs.
selected_plan.feedback_interpretation: H24 is strengthened as limited structural transfer: at 100 ul, m89 grows from 8.81/14.05 at 5/1 to 13.49/26.04 ml at 10/1, whereas m104 changes from 5.20/13.90 to 7.91/11.00. m86 retains steep 5/1 response across loading, but full invariance is rejected by a 50-to-150 ul change of -5.25/-1.31 ml; completion is comparatively stable while onset advances. These questions now have lower marginal priority. H18 requires revision: transfer of m194's completion decline to 50 ul is rejected by its rising 10.34/14.73/21.52 ml sequence across 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1, unlike the 100 ul 36.18-to-28.27 decline. The actual m20 baseline is now measured and connects an increasing fixed-50 ul curve; the older m148 attribution remains discarded. m106 supports stronger later growth rather than the historically forecast early rise. H13 gains qualified support: m61's 2/1-to-10/1 onset change is -2.32 ml at 50 ul and -9.30 at 100 ul, while completion changes are similar at -4.63 and -4.75 ml. This rejects a large loading-invariant inverse onset response and supports separate endpoint interactions. H15 is refined by modest m25 growth through 10/1 before its large 50/1 anchor and opposite historical completion-error signs across m25, m82 and m95, rejecting a shared beta-ketoester correction. H25's initial m45 and m96 curve questions are substantially answered. H17's proposed large early lactone completion tail is unsupported: m181 at 50 ul measures 6.18/10.19, 7.38/13.29 and 21.45/31.79 ml at 1/1, 2/1 and 10/1, leaving a specific intermediate-ratio question. m177 still rejects smooth loading interpolation, but available lower-ratio inputs cannot replicate its exceptional high-ratio minima. Repeated short m92 EA completion supports a local association while PE-side repeatability remains unresolved. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over their measured ranges. All measured findings come from observed-table records; historical residuals describe past failures and candidate matches remain predictions only. No new labels, validation/test truth or external trajectory information were used.
